newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper vulnerable to further declines.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper vulnerable to further declines.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
The copper market may consolidate on Thursday, but remains vulnerable to further falls, technical analysts said.
The recent selling that has dented chart sentiment might see copper fall to $2,300 a tonne.
Aluminium's late rally on Wednesday may spark consolidation and possibly an upside break.

COPPER - Declining charts, option-related selling and rising London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks in the slow summer period were likely to keep the copper market on the defensive, but some consolidation might be seen, chartists and traders said.
"Technically copper remains vulnerable to further downside pressure, though having already fallen significantly a period of consolidation may be on the cards," Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said.

On Wednesday copper went into free-fall after breaking below support at $2,400 a tonne, hitting a seven-week low of $2,355. Traders expected that level to hold on Thursday but did not rule out a further downside move towards $2,300 in the near term.
Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading said falls to $2,325/$2,300 and possibly lower could be seen if $2,355 failed to hold .
On the upside copper was likely to struggle to overcome $2,390, followed by $2,400.
At 0720 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,390, versus London's Thursday late close of $2,365/70.
ALUMINIUM - The ability of the market to recover from a downside probe below $1,545 on Wednesday might signal a bounce, despite the lower trending copper market.

"The close is constructive and suggestive of further upside challenges," Squires of Wolff said. "However, with the technical indicators drifting sideways, further consolidation may be yet seen above $1,550," he added.
"This market may have done enough on the downside for the time being and inroads into resistance up,to $1,600 could be seen," Creates said.
At 0720 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,575, against $1,565/68.
